2_motivation:
The websearcher's verdict forbids the obvious card and names
the one that is open: D1 ("FiLM/modulation-conditioned spectral (FNO) decoder:
condition -> latent -> HF field, no field input") is **`preempted`** —
"Nothing mechanism-level. Admissible only as a *measurement/baseline arm* on
this panel against the mandatory floor arms" — and D3 is
**`preempted-but-MF-composition-open`**: "(i) the barrier diagnostic has never
been instantiated where the unobserved driver is a *stored coarse solve*,
making the floor validatable rather than assumed; (ii) NN-in-condition /
train-mean / zero as a standing certification panel is not done in the fetched
benchmark literature." This card therefore (a) declares the D1 decoder as its
baseline architecture, not its contribution; (b) adds the one regime-specific
element the data demands — a **condition-predicted amplitude head** — which is
the exact successor round 1 named when s5_tuning closed ("(i) a PREDICTED scale
head", `round1/experiment_cards/s5_tuning/batch_3/B3.json` part 7, where the
LF-proxy scaler reached nRMSE 0.367721 on helmholtz but the true-scale oracle
reached 0.258380 = skill 0.864 under the corrected denominator, and where 60%
of the damage was the amplitude channel per the two-gate rule); and (c) frames
every number against the D3 certificate, computed in-job and training-free, so
ADR r2-0003's conditional-mean reality becomes a measured per-dataset ceiling
instead of an assumption.
3_description:
New from-scratch family `models_r2/r2s1_cond_decoder` —
condition-only forward signature, no field input at any stage of test, no
round-1 code vendored. Condition standardized on train statistics -> 16 random
Fourier features -> 128-wide MLP -> 16x16 latent seed grid; 4 FiLM-modulated
spectral blocks (hidden 64, `modes_cap` 16) with progressive Fourier upsampling
to the native HF grid (WORK_CAP 256); the decoder output is L2-normalized to a
unit **direction** field and multiplied by `exp(logamp)` from a separate
128-wide MLP **amplitude head** trained on `log||y||`. Loss = relative L2 with
a p25-median denominator floor (round-1 two-gate rule: lambda <= 1 always +
low-norm tail gate), AdamW lr 1e-3 / wd 1e-5 / cosine / batch 16 / grad-clip
1.0 / 200 epochs. **Two disjoint train-side folds** (10% model selection, 10%
blend calibration) — no test-split quantity is ever consulted (the round-1 D3
val_idx double-consumption caveat); when `N_train < 20` (ifc_poisson, N_hf = 5)
the blend switches to leave-one-out and training to fixed-epoch, no early stop.
Final prediction = `lambda * model + (1 - lambda) * b` with `b` in {zero,
train_mean, nn_condition} and `lambda` on a 21-point grid, both chosen on the
calibration fold. Emitted splits: `test_hf` (scored, blended arm) plus
non-scored `ref_raw` (lambda = 1, same checkpoint — free), `ref_pod_lin`
(rank-50 POD + ridge, the declared D2 linear-reconstruction control, predicted
in advance to fail on the 4 discontinuous datasets per Lanthaler 2210.01074),
`ref_zero` / `ref_train_mean` / `ref_nn_condition` (floor arms recomputed
in-job and asserted equal to `state/anchors/floors.json` within 1e-9 — a seam
check, NOT a re-certification of r2s4's floors), and `cert_*` (the D3
certificate: aleatoric estimate from condition-pair differences with a
distance-slope test and zero-distance extrapolation, a `no_support` verdict
when the nearest pair distance exceeds 0.5 — `sharp__cahn_hilliard` will trip
it at 2.822 — the implied maximum achievable skill per dataset, and the
**LF-carrier cosine** between block-mean HF pair differences and train-LF pair
differences). Guards run at contract tier (2 epochs). Extra split names
deliberately avoid the `test*` prefix because
`eval/score_panel.py::_extract_test_metric` errors on ambiguous test splits.

expected_falsification:
H-r2s1-B1 ("a from-scratch condition->HF decoder
that predicts the per-sample amplitude from the condition and is blended
out-of-fold onto the best training-free floor extracts information the floors
do not have, and its residual gap is bounded by a measurable identifiability
floor") is FALSIFIED if, at 200 epochs / seed 0 on the stripped view, the
primary `test_hf` arm's panel geomean skill is `> 19.60` (i.e. fails to beat
the frozen best-floor anchor 23.0636 by 15%), **or** it fails to beat the best
frozen floor by >= 25% on BOTH `sharp__cahn_hilliard` (needs `<= 17.39`) and
`sharp__allen_cahn_2d` (needs `<= 201.90`) — the two datasets the in-job
certificate says have real headroom — **or** it is worse than 1.15x the best
frozen floor on any scored panel dataset (`sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d`
`> 68.78`, `sharp__fisher_kpp_2d` `> 13.79`, `sharp__allen_cahn_2d` `> 309.58`,
`sharp__cahn_hilliard` `> 26.66`, `ifc_poisson` `> 11.56`), which the
out-of-fold blend is designed to make impossible and would therefore indict the
calibration; `ext__helmholtz_2d` carries a report-only prediction (`<= 2.00`
with the zero-floor column) and no falsification weight, and every number is
labelled `provisional-single-seed`.

HYPERPARAMETER PROVENANCE. Every knob in config.RECIPE_ENV is transcribed verbatim from recipe.env and is ALSO passed through score_panel.py --env by scripts/01_train_eval.sh (so it enters code_hash); the five '_'-prefixed recipe keys are card directives and are deliberately excluded (starter handoff). Values not fixed by the card, all documented in code comments + the builder handoff: (1) R2S1_DENOM_FLOOR='p25_median' implemented as the p25 quantile of ||y|| over the fitting subset — the round-1 rule (s7_loss-B2 F9 / part-7 two-gate rule) names a BAND [p25, median] and F9 states 'p25 is where the concentration stops being pathological'; the lower edge is taken and a TBD comment in train.py::denominator_floor names 'median' as the other admissible reading, selectable through the same knob. (2) RFF frequency matrix B ~ N(0,1) (canonical unit-bandwidth RFF on standardized inputs), drawn from the run seed. (3) GELU nonlinearity + 1x1 local path beside each spectral path (standard FNO block layout, Li 2010.08895). (4) FiLM and amplitude output layers zero-initialised (gamma=1, beta=0, logamp = mean log||y||_train at init). (5) POD-ridge alpha selected by train-side K-fold CV over a fixed logspace(-6,2,9) grid rather than a hand-picked constant. (6) Fourier transforms use norm='forward' on both directions so the resolution cascade is amplitude-preserving band-limited interpolation.

DEVIATION FROM THE LITERAL RECIPE, flagged for the reviewer: the D3 certificate fits s^2 = a + b d^2 (R2S1_CERT_SLOPE_FIT='linear_on_sq', as fixed) on the R2S1_CERT_PAIRS=1000 CLOSEST condition pairs rather than 1000 random pairs. FLAGGED ITEM 1 - certificate deviation (closest 1000 pairs vs random 1000): SCIENTIFICALLY SOUND IN DIRECTION AND PROPERLY DISCLOSED (build_notes #7, builder handoff, a 20-line certificate.py module-docstring rationale, and pairs_used='closest' emitted in every result JSON). Selection is on the regressor d, not the response s, so it does not bias the OLS intercept; the estimand is a d->0 limit for which a local window is the right estimator; the random-pair global fit is misspecified because s^2 saturates near 2, biasing the intercept UP. It CANNOT bias any card claim: cert_* is not a test split (score_panel scores test_hf only) and every falsification threshold is a pre-registered constant, so there is no circularity. HOWEVER the estimate is window-dependent and not converged - reviewer-measured aleatoric (train split only, 250/1000-recipe/4000/16000 closest, random-1000): helmholtz 0.000/1.200/1.772/1.921/2.013; pfc 0.428/0.522/0.487/0.487/0.506; allen_cahn 0.334/0.315/0.417/0.471/1.072; fisher_kpp 0.236/0.251/0.250/0.251/0.248; cahn_hilliard 0.882/0.696/0.665/0.654/0.758. The builder's rationale reproduces exactly (allen_cahn random 1.072 vs closest 0.315). pfc and fisher_kpp are window-robust and quotable; allen_cahn moves ~50% and must be quoted as a range; ext__helmholtz_2d is PATHOLOGICAL - at the recipe's 1000 pairs it reports an aleatoric floor of 1.200, worse than the zero predictor (1.0) on the one panel dataset the card calls deterministic, and it will be stamped verdict='supported'/trustworthy=true because the support gate tests d_min (0.035) rather than the width of the window actually fitted (d_used_max). That value already sits unremarked in build_notes #2 as cert_identifiability 1.2002501. The gate matches card part 3 verbatim, so this is a locked-card design limit, not builder drift. MANDATORY for the analyzer: do not report helmholtz implied_max_skill as a ceiling (cite the zero-floor column per section 12.1); report allen_cahn as a range. ZERO-COST RECOVERY: certify() is training-free and train-split-only, so the whole sensitivity table can be regenerated offline at analysis time with no rerun - which is why this is SUGGEST and not FAIL. Optional cheap-now fix: emitting intercept_s2 at several windows is ~6 additive lines contradicting no locked field, free before submit but a full panel rerun afterwards (code_hash change invalidates the cache).

FLAGGED ITEM 2 - TBD R2S1_DENOM_FLOOR=p25_median implemented as p25: ACCEPTABLE, TRACEABLE AND INERT FOR EVERY REPORTED NUMBER. train.py:36-55 takes the lower (more conservative, fewer-samples-clipped) edge of the round-1 band with a TBD marker naming median and both readings selectable through the same knob; declared in build_notes #6 and the builder handoff. interpretation: I1 (high confidence; T1-F2/F4, T2-F1/F2/F3, T3-F8) -- THE ARCHITECTURE IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. The scored arm is information-limited, not representation-limited: the condition determines 1-3 out-of-fold degrees of freedom per dataset, and a <=156-parameter closed-form head in the same condition featurization reproduces the panel geomean to within half a min_claimable_effect. Turn 3 removes the headline exception: after an out-of-fold six-scalar band calibration the tiny head matches or beats the shipped decoder on ext__helmholtz_2d, sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d (residual 0.06%), sharp__allen_cahn_2d and sharp__fisher_kpp_2d. The 13.7-15.9M parameters, the FiLM-spectral blocks, the progressive Fourier upsampling and the 200 epochs of SGD buy nothing measurable on those four; sharp__cahn_hilliard (+4.6% for the decoder under a coarser calibration) is the single surviving candidate for a real capacity benefit and is the card's sharpest open question.

I2 (high confidence; T3-F2/F4/F8) -- WHAT THE DECODER ACTUALLY DID ON pfc WAS SHRINK, NOT REGISTER. Turn-2's H3 predicted a phase/registration DOF; both arms have ring phase cosine ~0 and gain identically from an oracle circular shift, so no such DOF exists. The decoder simply emits 100x less energy in the one band whose phase is unpredictable. Shrinkage is a calibration property with one number attached to it, which is exactly why one scalar per band reproduces it.

I3 (high confidence; T3-F5/F6/F7) -- pfc's CONDITION->HF MAP IS A MEAN-LEVEL REGRESSION PLUS A PHASE-RANDOM PATTERN, both now quantified. The 2-dim condition determines the spatial mean (OOF R^2 0.99969) and the nucleation state (AUC 0.9998) and determines nothing else; on patterned samples the DC-only arm sits at the DC oracle to 6e-6. This is ADR r2-0003's conditional-mean barrier localized to a Fourier band and a sample class, and it bounds pfc skill at ~47 with this condition vector (pfc denominator caveat, copylf_baselines._notes.pfc, applies).

I4 (high confidence; T2-F5, T3-F8) -- UNDER A PER-SAMPLE RELATIVE METRIC WITH AN UNIDENTIFIABLE COMPONENT, THE SCORED QUANTITY REWARDS PREDICTING LESS, AND CORRECTLY CHOSEN CENTERING. Every sharp dataset's out-of-fold band calibration drives all non-DC gains to zero; helmholtz's drives a uniform ~0.25 shrink; and the helmholtz rescue that the card credited to a learned amplitude head is a zero-parameter re-centering in (unit direction, log amplitude) coordinates. All three levers that moved this card's numbers -- centering, band shrinkage, the blend lambda -- are calibration of a low-dimensional predictor. None is architecture.

I5 (medium confidence; T3-F9) -- THE METRIC'S JENSEN GAP DECIDES THE pfc VERDICT. The decoder's +6.9% exists in mean-of-rel-L2 and reverses in mean-of-energy (0.30764 vs 0.29612), so a capacity claim on pfc is a claim about the SHAPE of the per-sample error distribution (broad small wins, a worse tail), not about total error. Worth stating because the round scores the former.

I6 (medium confidence; T2-F6) -- THE BLEND lambda IS A SYMPTOM, NOT A DEFECT. lambda* tracks the arm's out-of-fold quality relative to the best floor rather than any dataset property (with the tiny head substituted, allen_cahn moves 0.40 -> 0.85, helmholtz's RAW arms are driven to 0.00 while FACT arms get 0.15). The calibration is behaving as designed; the bimodality flagged by the initial analyzer needs no fix.
6_analysis.falsification_postmortem: The clause fired on leg 1 only (panel geomean 19.6444 > 19.60) by 0.0444 skill units -- 26x below the certified panel min_claimable_effect 1.1419 -- while legs 2 and 3 did not fire. The mechanism-level reading is that leg 1's verdict was decided by noise around a threshold the card set at exactly 0.85x the anchor, and that the architecture hypothesis it was written to test was never the binding question. Turn 2 showed the identical protocol run with a 156-parameter closed-form head scores 19.0553, i.e. leg 1 would NOT have fired for a model with 1e5 fewer parameters; turn 3 showed the last dataset where the decoder was genuinely ahead (pfc, +6.9%) is a 0.06% gap once a six-scalar out-of-fold band calibration is applied to the tiny head. So the hypothesis 'a from-scratch condition->HF decoder that predicts the per-sample amplitude from the condition and is blended out-of-fold onto the best training-free floor extracts information the floors do not have' is CONFIRMED in its floors clause (the arm beats the best floor on all six datasets, geomean -14.8% vs the anchor) and FALSIFIED in its implicit architecture clause (nothing the decoder extracts is unavailable to a ~10^2-parameter closed form). The card's second claim -- 'its residual gap is bounded by a measurable identifiability floor' -- is upheld in substance but NOT by the card's own D3 pair-difference certificate, which the reviewer flagged as loose and which on helmholtz returns an aleatoric estimate (1.2002) above the zero predictor (1.0). Turns 1 and 3 established the bound non-parametrically instead: per-mode out-of-fold R^2 (turn 1) and, on pfc, a DC-only arm sitting at the DC oracle to 6e-6 on the patterned class (turn 3).
surprises: The declared-to-fail D2 control beat the scored arm, and the predicted-in-advance reason was wrong on both mechanism and dataset. ref_pod_lin (rank-50 POD+ridge) was predicted per Lanthaler arXiv:2210.01074 to fail on the four DISCONTINUOUS sharp datasets; it is within 1.05x of the scored arm on pfc/fisher_kpp/cahn_hilliard and BETTER on allen_cahn, and it blows up only on ext__helmholtz_2d -- the one SMOOTH panel dataset -- where turn-1 F6 identifies the cause as a 408x per-sample ||y|| spread interacting with the per-sample relative metric, not discontinuity.

The optimal calibrated form of the 14.4M-parameter decoder on pfc is gains [1,0,0,0,0,0]: a per-sample CONSTANT field. Zeroing every spatial structure the network produced improves it from 0.38396 to 0.37833, and an independent 35-parameter DC-only ridge does better still at 0.35020.

pfc is not one dataset but two: 44/100 test samples have essentially zero crystal-pattern energy (ring share p50 8.4e-6) and 44 have 62-75% of their energy in the pattern; the same arm scores 0.005988 on one class and 0.788299 on the other -- a 130x error-scale difference -- and the class is condition-predictable at OOF AUC 0.9998.

The card's own contribution (a condition-predicted amplitude head) helps exactly where the amplitude is NOT condition-predictable (helmholtz, log-amplitude OOF R^2 -0.103). It is doing re-centering, not prediction.

SEVERE EARLY OVERFIT was flagged by the initial analyzer as the most informative anomaly (best_epoch 2/4/6/24/2 of 200) and turned out to be a symptom rather than a cause: with only 1-3 identifiable degrees of freedom, epoch ~4 is where the optimizer has found them, and the remaining 196 epochs memorize an unidentifiable remainder. Fixing the overfit would not have changed the panel geomean by a min_claimable_effect.

7_gap_and_future.open_question: Is `sharp__cahn_hilliard`'s surviving decoder advantage REAL -- and is it the only place on this panel where capacity is worth anything? Every other panel dataset's apparent capacity benefit dissolved under an out-of-fold calibration of the ~150-parameter closed-form head: pfc +6.9% -> +0.06% (T3-F8), helmholtz +1.4% -> parity (0.92769 vs 0.92830), allen_cahn and fisher_kpp were already at or better than the decoder. `sharp__cahn_hilliard` did not dissolve, and turn 3 could only bound it (the full gain grid blew the 20-min script cap, so 0.56297 was quoted as an UPPER bound from an 11-gain x 1-pass calibration). The register turn re-ran the promoted, decomposition-based tool at the FULL 31-gain x 2-pass grid (75.5 s; `scratchpad/register_toolcheck_bandgain_cahn_hilliard.json`): gains [0, 0.9, 0, 1.5, 0.25, 0], calibrated+blended tiny head 0.55990 (skill 13.3937) against the shipped 0.53686 (skill 12.8425) -- a 4.29% / 0.5511-skill gap, i.e. 6.0x cahn_hilliard's certified single-dataset min_claimable_effect 0.09125 (`state/noise_floor.json`). So at one seed the gap is RESOLVABLE and is this card's one unexplained capacity benefit. Which of three mechanisms it is remains open: (i) genuine representation value in the 13.7-15.9 M-parameter decoder; (ii) an artifact of the tiny head's arm SET -- the calibration selected FACT-2 there, and cahn_hilliard is the dataset where the factorized centering is most wrong (ratio ||mean field|| / geo-mean||y|| = 0.052, T2-F5), while its band gains are the panel's only non-shrinking set; (iii) rank starvation of the closed form -- cahn_hilliard is the ONE panel dataset with 3 condition-identifiable POD modes (T1-F2) and a 19-dim condition on which r2s4-B1's aleatoric ceiling returns `no_support`, so a head capped at r<=3 may simply be too small. A rank sweep of the closed-form head at r = 3..20 with the band gains, all fitted out of fold and training-free, decides between (i) and (ii)/(iii) in minutes -- `tools/condition_identifiable_rank.py --datasets sharp__cahn_hilliard` plus `tools/band_gain_counterfactual.py` is exactly that experiment.
7_gap_and_future.next_direction: Stop buying decoder capacity in this stream; spend B2 on IDENTIFICATION and CALIBRATION, which is where every number this card moved actually came from (T3-I3). Concretely, for r2s1_direct-B2: (1) The scoreable-arm form should be SELECTED by measurable, training-free dataset statistics rather than fixed by architecture: centering by `ratio_meanfield_over_geoamp` (>>1 -> unit-direction x amplitude, which is worth 3.82x on helmholtz for ZERO learned parameters; <<1 -> plain additive, since factorizing costs 1.8x on allen_cahn, T2-F5); rank by the identifiable-mode count (T1-F2: 1-5 modes, i.e. r<=3 everywhere except possibly cahn_hilliard); and a per-band out-of-fold shrinkage stage (T3-F8), which on every sharp dataset except cahn_hilliard zeroes ALL non-DC bands. (2) The DC-only arm (one ridge, ~35 fitted parameters, a per-sample CONSTANT field) must be added to the family's floor set: on pfc it scores 0.35020 against the 14.4 M-parameter decoder's 0.38403 and sits at the DC oracle to 6e-6 on the patterned class (T3-F6/T3-F7), so any arm that does not beat it is measuring mean-level regression. (3) Any capacity claim B2 wants to make has to be made on `sharp__cahn_hilliard` and against a BAND-CALIBRATED competitor, not a raw one -- that is the only cell of the panel still open (see open_question). 7_gap_and_future.cross_stream_notes: INFORMATION-LIMIT CONVERGENCE -- three streams measured the same ceiling with three unrelated estimators, and they agree dataset by dataset. (a) This card (HF side, POD coefficients): the number of POD modes whose coefficient has 5-fold out-of-fold R^2 > 0.1 from the condition is helmholtz 5, pfc 2, allen_cahn 1, fisher_kpp 1, cahn_hilliard 3, ifc_poisson 1; past mode 1-2 the out-of-fold R^2 is NEGATIVE, while a 50-mode train basis represents the TEST fields to 0.0033-0.0672 nRMSE on 4 of 6 (T1-F2/T1-F4). (b) r2s4_diag-B1 (energy side, training-free aleatoric barrier): its certifier sits within 1-14% of the k-NN/pair barrier on fisher_kpp, allen_cahn and pfc, and its part 7 already names cahn_hilliard + ifc_poisson as the datasets where the barrier has `no_support`. (c) r2s2_stacked-B1 turn 2 F7 (LF side): the number of LF-field PCs whose coefficient is learnable from the condition is 1 on pfc / allen_cahn / fisher_kpp and 3 on cahn_hilliard, and the trained emulator's own output rank matches it (rank-1 collapse where 1 PC is learnable; rank-22 on cahn_hilliard). The same rank ladder therefore appears on the HF fields (this card) and on the LF fields (r2s2), independently, and matches r2s4's energy-side barrier ordering. Four consequences other streams should act on: (1) BEFORE a card claims value for capacity/architecture, run `tools/condition_identifiable_rank.py` and beat a ~10^2-parameter closed-form head -- here a 156-parameter head matched a 15,878,402-parameter arm's panel geomean to 0.52x the min_claimable_effect (T2-F1/T2-F2). (2) Under the round's per-sample RELATIVE metric, the scored quantity rewards predicting LESS: out-of-fold band calibration drives all non-DC gains to zero on every sharp dataset and applies a uniform ~4x shrink on helmholtz (T3-F8) -- the same phenomenon as r2s4-B1's shrinkage oracle returning lambda* = 0 on helmholtz. Any stream shipping an uncalibrated arm is leaving that on the table, and any stream comparing two arms without calibrating both is measuring shrinkage, not architecture. (3) A per-sample CONSTANT field predicted from the condition (~35 parameters) beat the 14.4 M-parameter decoder on pfc (0.35020 vs 0.38403) and is at the DC oracle on the patterned class; treat it as a mandatory floor arm wherever the DC energy share is high. (4) pfc is TWO datasets (44/100 test samples patterned; the class is condition-predictable at out-of-fold AUC 0.9998) -- pooled pfc numbers mix a 0.79-nRMSE problem with a 0.006-nRMSE one, so per-class scoring is required before any pfc claim, in this or any stream.
